+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""What the target model can verify: per-layer spec capabilities.
+
+A speculator declares the plans it wants to verify (``SpecResources.plan_kind``).
+Each worker walks its layers after the attention backends are built and reports
+the highest plan kind every layer verifies correctly, with a reason for each
+layer or setting that lowers it (``SpecCapabilities``). The engine core reduces
+the reports of every rank, lets the speculator adapt its resources to them
+(``SpeculatorConfig.adapt_resources``) and hands the result to the scheduler and
+to every worker. A model whose layers cannot verify trees therefore runs a tree
+speculator as a chain; only a layer that cannot verify a chain at all (plan kind
+``"none"``) refuses speculative decoding.
+"""
+
+from collections import Counter
+from collections.abc import Iterable, Iterator, Mapping, Sequence
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, Literal, get_args
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.kernels import KernelRegistry
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.round import SpecResources
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.speculator_config import SpeculatorConfig
+    from vllm.v1.worker.utils import AttentionGroup
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+PlanKind = Literal["none", "chain", "tree", "mask"]
+"""The plans a model verifies, in increasing order: ``"none"`` (no speculative
+decoding), ``"chain"`` (each row follows the one before it), ``"tree"`` (each
+row names its parent row and sees its ancestors), ``"mask"`` (a tree whose rows
+may also carry their own visibility mask, ``VerifyPlan.mask``)."""
+
+PLAN_KINDS: tuple[PlanKind, ...] = get_args(PlanKind)
+
+
+def plan_kind_rank(kind: PlanKind) -> int:
+    """The position of ``kind`` in :data:`PLAN_KINDS`."""
+    return PLAN_KINDS.index(kind)
+
+
+def min_plan_kind(kinds: Iterable[PlanKind]) -> PlanKind:
+    """The lowest of ``kinds``; the highest plan kind when there are none."""
+    return min(kinds, key=plan_kind_rank, default=PLAN_KINDS[-1])
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class SpecLayerKind:
+    """What a layer is to speculative decoding, derived from the KV cache spec
+    or the layer class (a plugin cannot invent one)."""
+
+    family: Literal["attn", "mamba", "layout"]
+    variant: str
+    """attn: the ``KVCacheSpecKind`` value; mamba: the layer class's
+    ``spec_layer_variant``; layout: what a commit moves,
+    ``"paged_token"`` (KV of one tensor per layer, any element size),
+    ``"paged_split_scale"`` (KV with separate scales: nvfp4, per-token-head) or
+    ``"mamba_state"``."""
+    state_mode: str = ""
+    """mamba and layout ``mamba_state`` only: how drafts keep recurrent state,
+    ``"slots"``, ``"replay"`` or ``"recover"``."""
+
+    def key(self) -> str:
+        suffix = f"@{self.state_mode}" if self.state_mode else ""
+        return f"{self.family}:{self.variant}{suffix}"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class SpecLimit:
+    """A layer kind or a setting that caps the plan kind, and why."""
+
+    plan_kind: PlanKind
+    reason: str
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class SpecCapabilities:
+    """What a worker's layers verify; reduced over ranks by the engine core."""
+
+    plan_kind: PlanKind
+    """The lowest plan kind any layer or setting allows."""
+    limits: tuple[SpecLimit, ...] = ()
+    """Every cap below the highest plan kind, for the startup log."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_limits(cls, limits: Iterable[SpecLimit]) -> "SpecCapabilities":
+        limits = tuple(dict.fromkeys(limits))
+        return cls(
+            plan_kind=min_plan_kind(limit.plan_kind for limit in limits),
+            limits=limits,
+        )
+
+
+def reduce_spec_capabilities(
+    capabilities: Sequence[SpecCapabilities],
+) -> SpecCapabilities:
+    """Combine the reports of every rank: pipeline-parallel ranks hold
+    different layers, so the model verifies the lowest plan kind of any rank."""
+    return SpecCapabilities.from_limits(
+        limit for caps in capabilities for limit in caps.limits
+    )
+
+
+def spec_layers(
+    attn_groups: Iterable[Iterable["AttentionGroup"]], layers: Mapping[str, Any]
+) -> Iterator[tuple["AttentionGroup", str, Any, Any]]:
+    """``(group, name, spec, layer)`` for each target layer a speculative round
+    verifies: its attention group, KV cache spec and module. Draft layers,
+    hidden-state caches and encoder or cross attention (whose rows do not
+    attend to each other) are not verified.
+    """
+    from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+        CrossAttentionSpec,
+        EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec,
+        HiddenStateCacheSpec,
+        UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs,
+    )
+
+    skipped = (HiddenStateCacheSpec, EncoderOnlyAttentionSpec, CrossAttentionSpec)
+    for groups in attn_groups:
+        for group in groups:
+            for name in group.layer_names:
+                spec = group.kv_cache_spec
+                if isinstance(spec, UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs):
+                    spec = spec.kv_cache_specs[name]
+                layer = layers.get(name)
+                # A group's spec can come from a draft layer or a target layer
+                # alike, so the layer says whether it is a draft layer.
+                if getattr(layer, "is_draft_layer", False) or isinstance(spec, skipped):
+                    continue
+                yield group, name, spec, layer
+
+
+def mamba_state_mode(cache_config: Any) -> str:
+    """How recurrent layers keep the drafts' states."""
+    if cache_config.use_replayssm:
+        return "replay"
+    if cache_config.use_kda_recoverssm:
+        return "recover"
+    return "slots"
+
+
+def layer_spec_limits(
+    attn_groups: Iterable[Iterable["AttentionGroup"]],
+    layers: Mapping[str, Any],
+    mamba_state_mode: str,
+    kernels: "KernelRegistry | None" = None,
+) -> list[SpecLimit]:
+    """The plan kind caps of the target's layers, one per (layer kind, reason)
+    with its layer count.
+
+    A layer verifies what the spec kernels it needs support for it
+    (``KernelRegistry.plan_kind``; ``kernels`` defaults to the reference
+    kernels). An attention layer is further capped by what its metadata
+    builder's ``spec_verify_limit`` returns for the layer's features. A
+    recurrent layer (``MambaBase``) verifies nothing when its class sets
+    ``spec_chain_supported = False`` and chains when it declares no
+    ``spec_layer_variant``. Only the layers of :func:`spec_layers` count.
+    """
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.abstract import MambaBase
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.kernels import KernelRegistry, SpecLayerSpec
+
+    if kernels is None:
+        kernels = KernelRegistry()
+    # (plan kind, what the layers are, why) -> number of layers
+    num_layers: Counter[tuple[PlanKind, str, str]] = Counter()
+    for group, name, spec, layer in spec_layers(attn_groups, layers):
+        if isinstance(layer, MambaBase):
+            num_layers[_mamba_layer_limit(name, layer, kernels, mamba_state_mode)] += 1
+            continue
+        kind = attn_layer_kind(spec)
+        plan_kind, why = group.metadata_builders[0].spec_verify_limit(
+            **attn_layer_features(layer, spec)
+        )
+        kernel_kind, kernel_why = kernels.plan_kind(
+            SpecLayerSpec(name, kind, layer, layout=attn_layout(layer, spec))
+        )
+        if plan_kind_rank(kernel_kind) < plan_kind_rank(plan_kind):
+            plan_kind, why = kernel_kind, kernel_why
+        num_layers[(plan_kind, kind.key(), why)] += 1
+    return [
+        SpecLimit(plan_kind, f"{what}, {n} layer{'s' * (n != 1)}: {why}")
+        for (plan_kind, what, why), n in num_layers.items()
+        if plan_kind != PLAN_KINDS[-1]
+    ]
+
+
+def _mamba_layer_limit(
+    name: str, layer: Any, kernels: "KernelRegistry", state_mode: str
+) -> tuple[PlanKind, str, str]:
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.kernels import SpecLayerSpec
+
+    layer_cls = type(layer)
+    if not layer_cls.spec_chain_supported:
+        return ("none", layer_cls.__name__, "decodes one token per request")
+    variant = layer_cls.spec_layer_variant
+    if variant is None:
+        return ("chain", layer_cls.__name__, "declares no spec_layer_variant")
+    # The state mode is part of the key: the slots kernels read a state slot
+    # per draft row, which replay and recovery do not keep.
+    kind = SpecLayerKind("mamba", variant, state_mode)
+    plan_kind, why = kernels.plan_kind(
+        SpecLayerSpec(name, kind, layer, layout="mamba_state")
+    )
+    if plan_kind == "tree":
+        # A row's state folds in every ancestor along parent, so a recurrent
+        # layer cannot hide one: masks lower to trees unless its verify kernel
+        # itself verifies masks.
+        why += " (a recurrent state folds in every ancestor: no masks)"
+    return (plan_kind, kind.key(), why)
+
+
+def attn_layer_kind(spec: Any) -> SpecLayerKind:
+    """The kind of an attention layer with KV cache spec ``spec``."""
+    from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import get_kv_cache_spec_kind
+
+    return SpecLayerKind("attn", get_kv_cache_spec_kind(spec).value)
+
+
+def attn_layout(layer: Any, spec: Any) -> str:
+    """What committing an attention layer's accepted path moves: ``""`` for a
+    cache not paged by slot (its model keeps its own commit),
+    ``"paged_split_scale"`` for KV quantised with separate scales, else
+    ``"paged_token"``."""
+    from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import KVQuantMode, get_kv_quant_mode
+
+    if not getattr(spec, "uses_slot_mapping", True):
+        return ""
+    mode = get_kv_quant_mode(str(getattr(layer, "kv_cache_dtype", "auto")))
+    if mode == KVQuantMode.NVFP4 or mode.is_per_token_head:
+        return "paged_split_scale"
+    return "paged_token"
+
+
+def attn_layer_features(layer: Any, spec: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """The keyword arguments of ``AttentionMetadataBuilder.spec_verify_limit``
+    for an attention layer with KV cache spec ``spec``. Features the layer does
+    not have are None or False (e.g. a soft cap of 0 is no soft cap)."""
+    from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import SinkFullAttentionSpec
+
+    impl = getattr(layer, "impl", None)
+    return dict(
+        kv_cache_dtype=getattr(layer, "kv_cache_dtype", "auto"),
+        sliding_window=getattr(spec, "sliding_window", None)
+        or getattr(layer, "sliding_window", None),
+        has_sinks=bool(getattr(layer, "has_sink", False))
+        or isinstance(spec, SinkFullAttentionSpec),
+        logits_soft_cap=getattr(impl, "logits_soft_cap", None) or None,
+        has_alibi=getattr(impl, "alibi_slopes", None) is not None,
+        chunk_size=getattr(spec, "attention_chunk_size", None),
+        rswa_window=getattr(spec, "rswa_window", None),
+        kv_sharing_target=getattr(layer, "kv_sharing_target_layer_name", None),
+    )
+
+
+def resolve_spec_resources(
+    speculator_config: "SpeculatorConfig",
+    declared: "SpecResources",
+    capabilities: Sequence[SpecCapabilities],
+) -> "SpecResources":
+    """The resources speculation runs with: the speculator's declaration adapted
+    to what every rank verifies (``capabilities``, one per worker).
+
+    Logs one line per cap that lowers the declared plan kind. Raises when a
+    layer verifies no plans at all, and when the adapted resources exceed the
+    declared ones or the capabilities. A speculator that must not run with a
+    lower plan kind raises in its ``adapt_resources``.
+    """
+    caps = reduce_spec_capabilities(capabilities)
+    lowering = [
+        limit
+        for limit in caps.limits
+        if plan_kind_rank(limit.plan_kind) < plan_kind_rank(declared.plan_kind)
+    ]
+    if caps.plan_kind == "none":
+        raise ValueError(
+            "Speculative decoding is not supported by this model: "
+            + "; ".join(limit.reason for limit in lowering)
+        )
+    for limit in lowering:
+        logger.info(
+            "spec decode: %s -> %s (%s)",
+            declared.plan_kind,
+            limit.plan_kind,
+            limit.reason,
+        )
+    effective = speculator_config.adapt_resources(declared, caps)
+    validate_effective_resources(declared, effective, caps)
+    return effective
+
+
+def validate_effective_resources(
+    declared: "SpecResources", effective: "SpecResources", caps: SpecCapabilities
+) -> None:
+    """Check ``SpeculatorConfig.adapt_resources``: memory and graphs are sized
+    for ``declared``, so ``effective`` may only take less of them, and its plan
+    kind must be one every layer verifies."""
+    problems = []
+    if plan_kind_rank(effective.plan_kind) > plan_kind_rank(
+        min_plan_kind((declared.plan_kind, caps.plan_kind))
+    ):
+        problems.append(
+            f"plan_kind {effective.plan_kind!r} is above the declared "
+            f"{declared.plan_kind!r} or the model's {caps.plan_kind!r}"
+        )
+    if effective.max_candidates > declared.max_candidates:
+        problems.append(
+            f"max_candidates {effective.max_candidates} > declared "
+            f"{declared.max_candidates}"
+        )
+    extra_shapes = set(effective.capture_shapes) - set(declared.capture_shapes)
+    if extra_shapes:
+        problems.append(f"capture_shapes {sorted(extra_shapes, key=str)} not declared")
+    if problems:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "SpeculatorConfig.adapt_resources returned resources the model cannot "
+            "run: " + "; ".join(problems)
+        )

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Commit of a speculative round along the accepted path.
+
+Every verify row wrote its KV at the chain slot of its row index
+(``num_computed_tokens + row``). After acceptance the accepted rows of a plan that is
+not a chain are not a prefix of the rows, so :class:`KvCompactor` copies the KV of
+path row ``path[j]`` to chain slot ``j`` in every attention layer; the next step then
+sees the cache a chain round would have left. A chain plan's path is ``arange``: the
+commit moves nothing and launches nothing.
+
+The recurrent state of hybrid models commits by row index instead: the model state
+resumes from the state the last accepted row wrote (``accepted_row``), and
+:class:`ConvWindowAligner` gathers the path's conv inputs into the window the next
+step reads.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.output import SamplerOutput
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.capabilities import PlanKind
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.kernels import (
+    ABOVE_NONE,
+    CommitStep,
+    KernelContext,
+    SpecKernel,
+    SpecLayerSpec,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.round import AcceptResult
+
+
+def accept_result_of(
+    sampler_output: SamplerOutput, chain_path: torch.Tensor
+) -> AcceptResult:
+    """The round's :class:`AcceptResult`: the path the speculator's ``accept``
+    chose, else the chain's.
+
+    ``chain_path`` is the constant ``[R, C]`` table ``path[r, j] == j``; nothing is
+    computed, so a chain step pays no launch for the result.
+    """
+    sampled = sampler_output.sampled_token_ids
+    path = sampler_output.accept_path
+    if path is None:
+        path = chain_path[: sampled.shape[0], : sampled.shape[1]]
+    return AcceptResult(
+        path=path,
+        path_len=sampler_output.num_sampled,
+        sampled=sampled,
+    )
+
+
+def accepted_rows(result: AcceptResult, num_reqs: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """``[num_reqs]`` int32: the verify row whose recurrent state each request resumes
+    from, ``path[path_len - 1]`` (row 0 when nothing was committed)."""
+    last = (result.path_len[:num_reqs].to(torch.int64) - 1).clamp_(min=0)
+    return result.path[:num_reqs].gather(1, last.unsqueeze(1)).squeeze(1).int()
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class KvCacheLayout:
+    """Where token ``t`` of head ``h`` of plane ``p`` (K or V) of one layer lives:
+    ``(t // block_size) * stride_block + (t % block_size) * stride_slot
+    + h * stride_head + p * stride_plane``, ``head_dim`` contiguous elements."""
+
+    stride_block: int
+    stride_slot: int
+    stride_head: int
+    stride_plane: int
+    block_size: int
+    num_heads: int
+    num_planes: int
+    head_dim: int
+    dtype: torch.dtype
+
+
+def kv_cache_layout(kv_cache: torch.Tensor, num_blocks: int) -> KvCacheLayout:
+    """The layout of a layer's KV cache tensor as the attention backend views it.
+
+    Takes the logical shapes vLLM's backends use: ``[blocks, heads, block_size,
+    content]`` (K and V packed in the content, FlashAttention, FlashInfer,
+    FlexAttention), ``[2, blocks, block_size, heads, dim]``, ``[blocks, 2,
+    block_size, heads, dim]`` and ``[blocks, block_size, dim]`` (MLA); the strides
+    are the tensor's own, so a permuted physical order is read correctly. A packed
+    content row moves whole, so it is one plane of ``content`` elements.
+    """
+    shape, stride = kv_cache.shape, kv_cache.stride()
+    if kv_cache.dim() == 4 and shape[0] == num_blocks:
+        if stride[3] != 1:
+            raise NotImplementedError("KV compaction needs contiguous head dims")
+        _check_dtype(kv_cache.dtype)
+        return KvCacheLayout(
+            stride_block=stride[0],
+            stride_slot=stride[2],
+            stride_head=stride[1],
+            stride_plane=0,
+            block_size=shape[2],
+            num_heads=shape[1],
+            num_planes=1,
+            head_dim=shape[3],
+            dtype=kv_cache.dtype,
+        )
+    if kv_cache.dim() == 5 and shape[0] == 2 and shape[1] == num_blocks:
+        plane, block = 0, 1
+    elif kv_cache.dim() == 5 and shape[0] == num_blocks and shape[1] == 2:
+        block, plane = 0, 1
+    elif kv_cache.dim() == 3 and shape[0] == num_blocks:
+        if stride[2] != 1:
+            raise NotImplementedError("KV compaction needs contiguous head dims")
+        _check_dtype(kv_cache.dtype)
+        return KvCacheLayout(
+            stride[0], stride[1], 0, 0, shape[1], 1, 1, shape[2], kv_cache.dtype
+        )
+    else:
+        raise NotImplementedError(
+            f"KV compaction does not know the KV cache layout {tuple(shape)}"
+        )
+    if stride[4] != 1:
+        raise NotImplementedError("KV compaction needs contiguous head dims")
+    _check_dtype(kv_cache.dtype)
+    return KvCacheLayout(
+        stride_block=stride[block],
+        stride_slot=stride[2],
+        stride_head=stride[3],
+        stride_plane=stride[plane],
+        block_size=shape[2],
+        num_heads=shape[3],
+        num_planes=2,
+        head_dim=shape[4],
+        dtype=kv_cache.dtype,
+    )

+@triton.jit
+def _compact_kv_kernel(
+    layer_ptrs,  # [L] uint64: base address of each layer's KV cache
+    table_ptrs,  # [L] uint64: the layer's group block table, [num_reqs, max_blocks]
+    table_strides,  # [L] int64: row stride of that table
+    table_block_sizes,  # [L] int32: tokens per block of that table
+    count_ptr,  # [R] int32: verify rows per request, by batch row
+    seq_lens_ptr,  # [num_reqs] int32
+    path_ptr,  # [R, C] int32, by batch row
+    stride_path,
+    path_len_ptr,  # [R] int32, by batch row
+    stride_block,
+    stride_slot,
+    stride_head,
+    stride_plane,
+    block_size,  # tokens per block of the cache as the backend views it
+    NUM_HEADS: tl.constexpr,
+    DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    DIM_P: tl.constexpr,
+    DTYPE: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    b, layer, plane_head = tl.program_id(0), tl.program_id(1), tl.program_id(2)
+    plane = plane_head // NUM_HEADS
+    head = plane_head % NUM_HEADS
+    # The verify rows are the query's last rows, so row r sits at context + r.
+    context = tl.load(seq_lens_ptr + b) - tl.load(count_ptr + b)
+    base = tl.load(layer_ptrs + layer).to(tl.pointer_type(DTYPE))
+    table = tl.load(table_ptrs + layer).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int32))
+    table_row = table + b * tl.load(table_strides + layer)
+    table_block_size = tl.load(table_block_sizes + layer).to(tl.int64)
+    offset = head * stride_head + plane * stride_plane
+    dims = tl.arange(0, DIM_P)
+    # Path order: path[j] >= j, so a destination is only ever a source read earlier.
+    for j in range(1, tl.load(path_len_ptr + b)):
+        src = context + tl.load(path_ptr + b * stride_path + j)
+        dst = context + j
+        if src != dst:
+            src_block = tl.load(table_row + src // table_block_size).to(tl.int64)
+            dst_block = tl.load(table_row + dst // table_block_size).to(tl.int64)
+            src_token = src_block * table_block_size + src % table_block_size
+            dst_token = dst_block * table_block_size + dst % table_block_size
+            src_at = (
+                (src_token // block_size) * stride_block
+                + (src_token % block_size) * stride_slot
+                + offset
+            )
+            dst_at = (
+                (dst_token // block_size) * stride_block
+                + (dst_token % block_size) * stride_slot
+                + offset
+            )
+            values = tl.load(base + src_at + dims, mask=dims < DIM)
+            tl.store(base + dst_at + dims, values, mask=dims < DIM)
+            tl.debug_barrier()
+

+class KvCompactor(SpecKernel):

+    share one layout go in one launch. A layer that reads another layer's cache
+    (KV sharing) must not be bound: it would be compacted twice.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.launches: list[
+            tuple[KvCacheLayout, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]
+        ] = []

+    def supports(self, layer: SpecLayerSpec) -> frozenset[PlanKind]:

+            return frozenset()

+    def bind(self, ctx: KernelContext, layers: Sequence[SpecLayerSpec]) -> None:

+            ptrs[0].append(cache.data_ptr())
+            ptrs[1].append(table.data_ptr())
+            ptrs[2].append(table.stride(0))
+            ptrs[3].append(layer.block_size)

+                layout,
+                *(
+                    torch.tensor(values, dtype=dtype, device=ctx.device)
+                    for values, dtype in zip(ptrs, dtypes)

+            )

+    def commit(self, step: CommitStep) -> None:

+        ``seq_lens[b]``."""

+                layer_ptrs.shape[0],

+                table_sizes,

+                result.path.stride(0),

+                layout.stride_block,
+                layout.stride_slot,
+                layout.stride_head,

+                NUM_HEADS=layout.num_heads,
+                DIM=layout.head_dim,

+# Names, resolved at launch: where vLLM disables Triton, ``tl`` is a placeholder
+# without int8 / int16, and the runner imports this module.
+_BITS = {1: "int8", 2: "int16", 4: "int32"}

+def copies_dtype(dtype: torch.dtype) -> bool:
+    """Whether the compactor and the aligner copy caches of ``dtype``."""
+    return dtype.itemsize in _BITS

+def _check_dtype(dtype: torch.dtype) -> None:
+    if not copies_dtype(dtype):

+@triton.jit
+def _align_conv_window_kernel(
+    window_ptrs,  # [L] uint64: base of each layer's conv state, viewed [slot, dim, tok]
+    table_ptrs,  # [L] uint64: the layer group's block table, batch rows
+    table_strides,  # [L] int64
+    path_ptr,  # [R, C] int32
+    stride_path,
+    path_len_ptr,  # [R] int32
+    stride_slot,
+    stride_dim,
+    stride_tok,
+    dim,
+    WIDTH: tl.constexpr,  # conv kernel width k
+    DTYPE: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    b = tl.program_id(0)
+    layer = tl.program_id(1)
+    length = tl.load(path_len_ptr + b)
+    if length <= 0:
+        return
+    last = tl.load(path_ptr + b * stride_path + length - 1)
+    table = tl.load(table_ptrs + layer).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.int32))
+    slot = tl.load(table + b * tl.load(table_strides + layer)).to(tl.int64)
+    if slot <= 0:  # the null block: a request without state in this group
+        return
+    feats = tl.program_id(2) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = feats < dim
+    base = (
+        tl.load(window_ptrs + layer).to(tl.pointer_type(DTYPE))
+        + slot * stride_slot
+        + feats * stride_dim
+    )
+    # Column (k-2)+j holds the conv input of row j (j < 0: the history). The next
+    # step reads the k-1 columns ending at (k-2)+last, which must hold the path's
+    # inputs: path[length-1-i], or the history once the path is exhausted. The path
+    # is increasing, so a source never lies above its destination nor at a column
+    # already written; descending destinations make the copy safe in place.
+    for i in tl.static_range(WIDTH - 1):
+        j = length - 1 - i
+        row = tl.where(
+            j >= 0, tl.load(path_ptr + b * stride_path + tl.maximum(j, 0)), j
+        )
+        value = tl.load(base + (WIDTH - 2 + row) * stride_tok, mask=mask)
+        tl.store(base + (WIDTH - 2 + last - i) * stride_tok, value, mask=mask)

+"""The kernels speculative decoding adds to verify and commit, by key.

+A spec kernel serves one :data:`KernelKey`: a layer kind (``SpecLayerKind.key()``)
+and an op.
+
+- ``verify`` runs the convolution and recurrence of a recurrent layer's
+  spec-decode rows (keys ``"mamba:<variant>@<state mode>"``). The layer calls it
+  from its forward, so it runs inside the captured decode graphs.
+- ``commit`` moves what the accepted path wrote to where the next step reads it
+  (``"layout:paged_token"`` for attention KV, ``"layout:mamba_state@<state
+  mode>"`` for recurrent state). The runner calls it after acceptance on a step
+  whose plan is not a chain; a chain commits nothing.
+
+:class:`KernelRegistry` is :class:`ReferenceKernels` overlaid by the providers
+the speculator names in ``SpeculatorConfig.spec_kernel_providers``, in order: a
+later provider wins a key. The registry also decides what the target verifies:
+a layer verifies the highest plan kind that every kernel it needs
+(:meth:`KernelRegistry.required_keys`) supports for it, and a chain when one is
+missing. So a provider may supply any subset of keys; a key it leaves out keeps
+the reference kernel, or lowers the plan kind when there is none, and a missing
+kernel is never called.
+

+
+    class MyGDNVerify(SpecKernel):
+        def supports(self, layer):
+            return frozenset({"chain", "tree"})
+

+

+        name = "my_provider"
+

+
+        def kernels(self):
+            return {("mamba:gdn@slots", "verify"): MyGDNVerify()}
+
+
+    class MySpeculatorConfig(SpeculatorConfig):

+"""The layout a :class:`VerifyPlan` gives the target's verify forward.
+
+Each request verifies the last ``count[b]`` rows of its query; row 0 of those is the
+root. The runner computes the batch's positions and slot mappings as for a chain
+(``num_computed_tokens + i``) and keeps the slot mappings: every row writes its KV at
+the chain slot of its row index, and the commit compacts the accepted path afterwards.
+For a plan that is not a chain, :meth:`PlanLayout.apply` then moves each row's
+position to ``num_computed_tokens + depth`` (or ``+ VerifyPlan.positions``) and
+computes its ancestor set (bit ``j`` set iff row ``j`` is the row or one of its
+ancestors), which tree attention reads, and, for a layout with a mask buffer, the
+rows it sees (``VerifyPlan.mask`` in the same bits, else the ancestor set), which
+custom-mask attention reads.
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.round import VerifyPlan
+
+MAX_PLAN_ROWS = 64
+"""Rows per request a plan can have: one bit per row in an int64 ancestor set."""
+
+
+def chain_parents(
+    max_num_reqs: int, max_rows: int, device: torch.device
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The ``[R, C]`` parent table of a chain: ``parent[r, i] == i - 1``."""
+    rows = torch.arange(-1, max_rows - 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    return rows.expand(max_num_reqs, max_rows).contiguous()
+
+
+def chain_path(max_num_reqs: int, max_rows: int, device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The ``[R, C]`` accepted path of a chain: ``path[r, j] == j``."""
+    rows = torch.arange(max_rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    return rows.expand(max_num_reqs, max_rows).contiguous()
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _plan_layout_kernel(
+    parent_ptr,  # [R, C] int32, by batch row
+    stride_parent,
+    count_ptr,  # [R] int32, by batch row
+    tokens_ptr,  # [R, C] int32 candidate tokens, by batch row (unused unless TOKENS)
+    stride_tokens,
+    query_start_loc_ptr,  # [num_reqs + 1] int32
+    positions_ptr,  # [num_tokens] int64: chain positions in, plan positions out
+    input_ids_ptr,  # [num_tokens] int32: candidate rows take the plan's tokens
+    tree_parents_ptr,  # [num_tokens] int32 out: parent row within the request
+    tree_ancestors_ptr,  # [num_tokens] int64 out: rows seen, 0 = causal
+    pos_delta_ptr,  # [num_tokens] int32 out: plan position - chain position
+    plan_positions_ptr,  # [R, C] int32 position offsets (unused unless POSITIONS)
+    stride_plan_positions,
+    plan_mask_ptr,  # [R, C, C] bool rows seen (unused unless MASK)
+    stride_mask_r,
+    stride_mask_i,
+    stride_mask_j,
+    C: tl.constexpr,
+    CP: tl.constexpr,
+    TOKENS: tl.constexpr,
+    CHAIN: tl.constexpr,
+    POSITIONS: tl.constexpr,
+    MASK: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    b = tl.program_id(0)
+    query_start = tl.load(query_start_loc_ptr + b)
+    end = tl.load(query_start_loc_ptr + b + 1)
+    count = tl.load(count_ptr + b)
+    start = end - count
+    # Every token of the request first gets the chain layout (prefill tokens in
+    # front of the plan rows keep it).
+    for block in range(query_start, start, BLOCK):
+        offs = block + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+        in_query = offs < start
+        tl.store(tree_parents_ptr + offs, offs - query_start - 1, mask=in_query)
+        tl.store(tree_ancestors_ptr + offs, tl.zeros([BLOCK], tl.int64), mask=in_query)
+        tl.store(pos_delta_ptr + offs, 0, mask=in_query)
+
+    rows = tl.arange(0, CP)
+    is_row = rows < count
+    parents = tl.load(parent_ptr + b * stride_parent + rows, mask=rows < C, other=-1)
+
+    # Rows are ordered parent first, so one pass in row order sees every parent done.
+    depth = tl.zeros([CP], dtype=tl.int32)
+    ancestors = tl.full([CP], 1, dtype=tl.int64)
+    for r in range(1, C):
+        parent = tl.sum(tl.where(rows == r, parents, 0))
+        at_parent = rows == parent
+        depth = tl.where(rows == r, tl.sum(tl.where(at_parent, depth, 0)) + 1, depth)
+        own_bit = tl.cast(1, tl.int64) << r
+        ancestors = tl.where(
+            rows == r, tl.sum(tl.where(at_parent, ancestors, 0)) | own_bit, ancestors
+        )
+    # Chain position = context + row; plan position = context + depth, or context
+    # + the plan's own offset.
+    if POSITIONS:
+        offset_pos = tl.load(
+            plan_positions_ptr + b * stride_plan_positions + rows, mask=is_row, other=0
+        )
+    else:
+        offset_pos = depth
+    positions = tl.load(positions_ptr + start + rows, mask=is_row, other=0)
+    tl.store(positions_ptr + start + rows, positions - rows + offset_pos, mask=is_row)
+    tl.store(pos_delta_ptr + start + rows, offset_pos - rows, mask=is_row)
+    # Parent as a row of the request's query: the root continues the token before
+    # it (-1 when the root is the query's first token).
+    offset = start - query_start
+    local_parent = tl.where(parents >= 0, offset + parents, offset - 1)
+    tl.store(tree_parents_ptr + start + rows, local_parent, mask=is_row)
+    # A chain attends causally; a branching plan is the whole query (prefills
+    # verify chains only), so its bits index the request's query rows.
+    if CHAIN:
+        seen = tl.zeros([CP], tl.int64)
+    elif MASK:
+        # Row i sees row j <= i where mask[b, i, j]; its own bit is always set
+        # and later rows are never seen.
+        cols = tl.arange(0, CP)
+        lower = (cols[None, :] <= rows[:, None]) & (rows[:, None] < C)
+        lower = lower & (cols[None, :] < C)
+        sees = tl.load(
+            plan_mask_ptr
+            + b * stride_mask_r
+            + rows[:, None] * stride_mask_i
+            + cols[None, :] * stride_mask_j,
+            mask=lower,
+            other=0,
+        )
+        bits = tl.where((sees != 0) & lower, tl.cast(1, tl.int64) << cols[None, :], 0)
+        own = tl.cast(1, tl.int64) << rows
+        seen = tl.where(is_row, tl.sum(bits, axis=1) | own, 0)
+    else:
+        seen = ancestors
+    tl.store(tree_ancestors_ptr + start + rows, seen, mask=is_row)
+    if TOKENS:
+        is_candidate = is_row & (rows > 0)
+        tokens = tl.load(tokens_ptr + b * stride_tokens + rows, mask=is_candidate)
+        tl.store(input_ids_ptr + start + rows, tokens, mask=is_candidate)
+
+
+class PlanLayout:
+    """The batch's verify rows laid out per query token, in buffers CUDA graphs
+    replay, and the chain positions to put back after the forward.
+
+    Per query token: ``tree_parents`` (the parent as a row of the request's query,
+    -1 for the query's first token; a chain's ``i - 1`` for tokens that are not plan
+    rows), ``tree_ancestors`` (the query rows the row sees, as bits: the plan's
+    ``mask`` when it has one, else the row's ancestors; 0 for every token of a
+    chain: attend causally) and ``pos_delta`` (plan position minus chain position).
+    The first two are what ``CommonAttentionMetadata.tree_parents`` /
+    ``tree_ancestors`` point at.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        max_num_tokens: int,
+        max_rows: int,
+        device: torch.device,
+    ):
+        if max_rows > MAX_PLAN_ROWS:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"a verify plan has at most {MAX_PLAN_ROWS} rows per request, "
+                f"got {max_rows}"
+            )
+        self.max_rows = max_rows
+        self.tree_parents = torch.full(
+            (max_num_tokens,), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+        )
+        self.tree_ancestors = torch.zeros(
+            max_num_tokens, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+        )
+        self.pos_delta = torch.zeros(max_num_tokens, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+        self.chain_positions = torch.zeros(
+            max_num_tokens, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+        )
+        # Positions currently hold plan positions that ``restore_positions`` undoes.
+        self.applied = False
+
+    def apply(
+        self,
+        plan: VerifyPlan,
+        count: torch.Tensor,
+        query_start_loc: torch.Tensor,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor | None,
+        num_reqs: int,
+        num_tokens: int,
+        num_tokens_padded: int | None = None,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Turn ``positions`` from chain to plan positions, write the plan's
+        candidate tokens into ``input_ids`` (a plan with ``tokens``), and fill the
+        layout buffers for the first ``num_reqs`` batch rows. ``count`` is the
+        plan's count, or the rows per request of a chain the runner lays out."""
+        assert plan.parent.shape[1] <= self.max_rows
+        self.chain_positions[:num_tokens].copy_(positions[:num_tokens])
+        if num_tokens_padded is not None and num_tokens_padded > num_tokens:
+            self.tree_parents[num_tokens:num_tokens_padded].fill_(-1)
+            self.tree_ancestors[num_tokens:num_tokens_padded].zero_()
+            self.pos_delta[num_tokens:num_tokens_padded].zero_()
+        num_rows = plan.parent.shape[1]
+        tokens = plan.tokens if plan.tokens is not None and not plan.is_chain else None
+        assert tokens is None or input_ids is not None
+        plan_positions, mask = plan.positions, plan.mask
+        _plan_layout_kernel[(num_reqs,)](
+            plan.parent,
+            plan.parent.stride(0),
+            count,
+            tokens if tokens is not None else plan.parent,
+            tokens.stride(0) if tokens is not None else 0,
+            query_start_loc,
+            positions,
+            input_ids if input_ids is not None else positions,
+            self.tree_parents,
+            self.tree_ancestors,
+            self.pos_delta,
+            plan_positions if plan_positions is not None else plan.parent,
+            plan_positions.stride(0) if plan_positions is not None else 0,
+            mask if mask is not None else plan.parent,
+            mask.stride(0) if mask is not None else 0,
+            mask.stride(1) if mask is not None else 0,
+            mask.stride(2) if mask is not None else 0,
+            C=num_rows,
+            CP=triton.next_power_of_2(num_rows),
+            TOKENS=tokens is not None,
+            CHAIN=plan.is_chain,
+            POSITIONS=plan_positions is not None,
+            MASK=mask is not None,
+            BLOCK=256,
+            num_warps=1,
+        )
+        self.applied = True
+
+    def restore_positions(self, positions: torch.Tensor, num_tokens: int) -> None:
+        """Put the chain positions back after the forward: the sampler and the
+        drafter read them."""
+        if self.applied:
+            positions[:num_tokens].copy_(self.chain_positions[:num_tokens])
+            self.applied = False

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Types of the speculative round contract.
+
+A speculative step is a round: the speculator plans the rows the target verifies
+(:class:`VerifyPlan`), the target runs them, the speculator accepts a path through them
+(:class:`AcceptResult`) and the runner commits the KV and the recurrent state along that
+path. :class:`SpecResources` is what speculation holds, declared once at startup, and
+:class:`StepObservation` is the read-only record of each step.
+
+Everything a speculator hands the runner is either a frozen dataclass of host integers
+or a device tensor in a buffer the speculator owns and keeps alive for the step. The
+runner never reads a device value on the host.
+
+Shapes use ``R = max_num_reqs`` (indexed by batch row, the order of ``idx_mapping``)
+and ``C = SpecResources.max_candidates`` (rows per request, the root included).
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Sequence
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.capabilities import PlanKind
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.step_observation import (
+    StepObservation as _StepObservation,
+)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PlanShape:
+    """One target-forward shape the runner captures as a CUDA graph.
+
+    ``uniform_count`` rows per request when set (a chain's K + 1, or a fixed tree
+    width). None asks for a variable-length decode graph that takes any mix of
+    1..max_candidates rows per request.
+    """
+
+    uniform_count: int | None
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class SpecResources:
+    """What speculation holds.
+
+    The scheduler reserves ``max_candidates`` KV slots per decoding request and the
+    runner captures ``capture_shapes``.
+
+    The speculator's config declares them (``SpeculatorConfig.resources``), and the
+    KV and recurrent-state pools are sized for that declaration. The engine core then
+    lowers them, never raises them, to what the model's layers verify
+    (``SpeculatorConfig.adapt_resources``) and hands the result to the scheduler and
+    to every worker.
+    """
+
+    max_candidates: int
+    """Rows per request in a verify forward, the root row included (1 = plain decode).
+    The ceiling of every ``VerifyPlan.count``."""
+    capture_shapes: tuple[PlanShape, ...]
+    max_branching: int = 1
+    """1 for chains. Above 1 the attention backend and the linear-attention layers must
+    take a parent per row."""
+    custom_mask: bool = False
+    """Plans may carry ``VerifyPlan.mask``: the attention layers must take a
+    visibility mask per row. Needs ``max_branching > 1``."""
+
+    @property
+    def plan_kind(self) -> PlanKind:
+        """The plans the speculator verifies: masks when it declares
+        ``custom_mask``, trees when it branches, else chains."""
+        if self.custom_mask:
+            return "mask"
+        return "tree" if self.max_branching > 1 else "chain"
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if self.max_candidates < 1:
+            raise ValueError(f"max_candidates must be >= 1, got {self.max_candidates}.")
+        bad = [
+            shape.uniform_count
+            for shape in self.capture_shapes
+            if shape.uniform_count is not None
+            and not 1 <= shape.uniform_count <= self.max_candidates
+        ]
+        if bad:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"capture_shapes uniform counts {bad} are outside "
+                f"[1, max_candidates={self.max_candidates}]."
+            )
+        if self.max_branching < 1:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"max_branching ({self.max_branching}) must be >= 1: 1 is a chain."
+            )
+        if self.custom_mask and self.max_branching == 1:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "custom_mask needs max_branching > 1: a plan with a mask is laid "
+                "out as a tree"
+            )
+
+    @property
+    def uniform_counts(self) -> list[int]:
+        """The uniform rows per request of the listed shapes, ascending."""
+        return sorted(
+            {
+                s.uniform_count
+                for s in self.capture_shapes
+                if s.uniform_count is not None
+            }
+        )
+
+    @property
+    def varlen(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether a variable-length decode graph is listed."""
+        return any(s.uniform_count is None for s in self.capture_shapes)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class BudgetView:
+    """What the scheduler knows when it asks for the step's admission limit
+    (:meth:`SpeculatorConfig.admit_limit`) and candidate budget
+    (:meth:`SpeculatorConfig.candidate_budget`). Host integers. For the limit
+    they are read once the running requests are scheduled, before any waiting
+    one is admitted; for the budget, once all of this step's requests are
+    scheduled and their blocks allocated."""
+
+    num_scheduled_reqs: int
+    num_running: int
+    num_waiting: int
+    num_free_blocks: int
+    max_num_seqs: int
+    block_size: int
+    """Tokens per block of the unified pool (the scheduler's block size)."""
+
+
+@dataclass
+class VerifyPlan:
+    """The rows the target verifies this step, per scheduled request, as device tensors.
+
+    Row 0 of a request is the root: its last committed token, whose logits sample the
+    bonus token. Rows ``1..count-1`` are candidates; ``parent[r, i]`` is the row that
+    candidate ``i`` continues, in ``[0, i)``, so rows are ordered parent first and any
+    prefix of them is a plan too. A chain has ``parent[r, i] == i - 1``. Entries past
+    ``count[r]`` are ignored.
+
+    The runner derives from the plan the position of each row (``num_computed_tokens``
+    plus its depth, or plus ``positions``), the rows it sees (its ancestors, or
+    ``mask``), and its KV slot: every row writes its KV at the
+    chain slot of its row index, and the commit compacts the accepted path afterwards.
+
+    Buffers belong to whoever built the plan and stay valid until the commit returns,
+    so CUDA graph replays read stable addresses.
+    """
+
+    parent: torch.Tensor
+    """``[R, C]`` int32, ``parent[r, 0] == -1``."""
+    count: torch.Tensor | None
+    """``[R]`` int32 in ``[1, C]``; 1 is a plain decode. None only for the chain plan
+    the runner builds itself, whose counts are the scheduled drafts plus one."""
+    tokens: torch.Tensor | None = None
+    """``[R, C]`` int32 candidate tokens (``tokens[r, 0]`` is ignored: the root token is
+    known). None only for the runner's chain plan, whose tokens are in its draft
+    buffer."""
+    draft_probs: torch.Tensor | None = None
+    """``[R, C, vocab]`` float32 for probabilistic verification, else None."""
+    is_chain: bool = False
+    """Host flag set by the builder when every ``parent[r, i] == i - 1`` by
+    construction. The runner then runs the chain-only path: positions stay
+    ``num_computed_tokens + i``, no ancestor sets, no KV compaction. Never derived
+    from the device tensors."""
+    positions: torch.Tensor | None = None
+    """``[R, C]`` int32 position of each row as an offset from
+    ``num_computed_tokens``, replacing the row's depth; None places each row at its
+    depth. Positions do not enter a recurrence, so any model takes them. A row's KV
+    slot stays its row index."""
+    mask: torch.Tensor | None = None
+    """``[R, C, C]`` bool: ``mask[r, i, j]`` is whether row ``i`` sees row ``j``;
+    None sees the row's ancestors. ``mask[r, i, i]`` is taken as True and entries
+    with ``j > i`` are ignored (a row never sees a later row); the committed prefix
+    is always visible. Needs resources with ``custom_mask`` (plan kind
+    ``"mask"``). ``parent`` still gives the paths the commit accepts along, and the
+    recurrent layers of a hybrid model read ``parent``, not the mask."""
+
+    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
+        if not self.is_chain and (self.count is None or self.tokens is None):
+            raise ValueError("a plan that is not a chain must carry count and tokens")
+        if self.is_chain and (self.positions is not None or self.mask is not None):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "a chain plan has positions num_computed_tokens + i and causal "
+                "attention; a plan with positions or a mask is not a chain"
+            )
+        rows = self.parent.shape
+        if self.positions is not None and tuple(self.positions.shape) != tuple(rows):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"positions has shape {tuple(self.positions.shape)}, parent "
+                f"{tuple(rows)}"
+            )
+        if self.mask is not None and tuple(self.mask.shape) != (*rows, rows[1]):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"mask has shape {tuple(self.mask.shape)}, expected "
+                f"{(*rows, rows[1])} for parent {tuple(rows)}"
+            )
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PlanInputs:
+    """What the runner knows about a batch before its inputs are built, for
+    :meth:`BaseSpeculator.plan`. Host values, except ``idx_mapping``."""
+
+    req_ids: Sequence[str]
+    """The batch's requests in batch-row order. Stable across preemption, unlike
+    the state slots."""
+    idx_mapping: torch.Tensor
+    """``[num_reqs]`` int64 device tensor: the request state slot of each batch row."""
+    idx_mapping_np: np.ndarray
+    """``[num_reqs]`` host copy of ``idx_mapping``."""
+    scheduled_rows: np.ndarray
+    """``[num_reqs]`` int32: rows the scheduler reserved per request, 1 + its drafts."""
+    chain_only: bool
+    """The runner can only verify chains this step: a prefill is in the batch, a
+    logits processor reads each row's prefix (penalties, bad words, a thinking
+    budget, a custom processor), structured output, or a parallelism mode that does
+    not lay out other plans (pipeline, context parallel). The plan must then
+    be a chain; it may still verify fewer rows."""
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PlanBound:
+    """Host integers the runner needs before the device plan exists.
+
+    ``rows[r]`` is how many rows request ``r`` verifies, at most the
+    ``scheduled_rows[r]`` the scheduler reserved (1 + its drafts); the drafts past
+    it leave the batch and count as rejected. None verifies every scheduled row.
+    """
+
+    rows: np.ndarray | None = None
+
+
+@dataclass
+class VerifyOutput:
+    """What the target computed for the rows of the requests ``accept`` verifies,
+    in plan order. A large batch is verified in request ranges; every tensor here
+    and the plan ``accept`` gets cover the same range, indexed from 0."""
+
+    logits: torch.Tensor
+    """``[num_rows, vocab]`` raw logits after the LM head (and the grammar bitmask)."""
+    row_start: torch.Tensor
+    """``[num_reqs + 1]`` int32 cumulative row offsets of each request."""
+    idx_mapping: torch.Tensor
+    """``[num_reqs]`` request state slot of each request."""
+    idx_mapping_np: np.ndarray
+    expanded_idx_mapping: torch.Tensor
+    """``[num_rows]`` request state slot of each row."""
+    expanded_local_pos: torch.Tensor
+    """``[num_rows]`` row index within its request (its plan row)."""
+    positions: torch.Tensor
+    """``[num_rows]`` int64 plan position of each row: the request's committed
+    tokens plus the row's depth. Sampling noise and position-dependent logits
+    processing use it."""
+    drafted: torch.Tensor
+    """``[num_rows]`` int64 token each row holds (row 0: the last committed token); -1
+    for a row that must not be accepted (a placeholder or a grammar-rejected draft)."""
+    draft_tokens: torch.Tensor
+    """``[num_rows]`` the rows' real token ids, for logits processing."""
+    seq_lens_upper_bound_np: np.ndarray
+    """``[num_reqs]`` host upper bound of each request's sequence length."""
+
+
+@dataclass
+class AcceptResult:
+    """Which rows of each request the target confirmed, and the token that follows.
+
+    ``path[r, :path_len[r]]`` lists the accepted rows from the root (row 0) down, each
+    a child of the previous one, so ``path[r, j] >= j``. ``sampled[r, :path_len[r]]``
+    are the committed tokens: the accepted candidates' tokens followed by the bonus
+    token sampled from the logits of the last accepted row. The runner commits the KV
+    and the recurrent state along ``path``; every other row is rejected. Whether the
+    commit moves anything is the plan's ``is_chain``, not a property of the result.
+    """
+
+    path: torch.Tensor
+    """``[R, C]`` int32 row indices."""
+    path_len: torch.Tensor
+    """``[R]`` int32 in ``[1, C]``: the number of committed tokens (0 for a row that
+    sampled nothing, e.g. a prefill chunk that does not end its prompt)."""
+    sampled: torch.Tensor
+    """``[R, C]`` token ids."""
+    processed_logits: torch.Tensor | None = None
+    """``[num_rows, vocab]`` the logits after the sampling parameters, in row order,
+    when ``accept`` computed them: the runner takes processed logprobs and the
+    sampling mask of each committed token from its path row. None: the raw logits."""
+
+
+# Defined with observe_step (step_observation.py); re-exported as part of the
+# round's vocabulary.
+StepObservation = _StepObservation

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The speculative round as the GPU model runner drives it: plan, lay out,
+restore, commit and observe one verify step."""
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import async_tensor_h2d
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import AttentionSpec
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.capabilities import (
+    SpecCapabilities,
+    SpecLayerKind,
+    SpecLimit,
+    attn_layer_kind,
+    attn_layout,
+    layer_spec_limits,
+    mamba_state_mode,
+    spec_layers,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.commit import accept_result_of, accepted_rows
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.kernels import (
+    CommitStep,
+    KernelContext,
+    KernelRegistry,
+    SpecLayerSpec,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.plan_kernels import (
+    PlanLayout,
+    chain_parents,
+    chain_path,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.round import (
+    AcceptResult,
+    PlanBound,
+    PlanInputs,
+    SpecResources,
+    VerifyPlan,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.step_observation import StepObservation
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+    from vllm.v1.core.sched.output import SchedulerOutput
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils import BatchExecutionDescriptor
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.input_batch import InputBatch, InputBuffers
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner import GPUModelRunner
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.output import SamplerOutput
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.sampler import Sampler
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.speculator import BaseSpeculator
+
+
+class SpecRound:
+    """What the GPU model runner holds for speculative decoding besides the
+    speculator: the chain plan, the plan layout when the speculator branches,
+    the resources and capabilities it runs with, and the spec kernels. Built
+    only with speculative decoding."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+        resources: SpecResources,
+        max_num_reqs: int,
+        max_num_tokens: int,
+        num_speculative_steps: int,
+        device: torch.device,
+    ):
+        self.vllm_config = vllm_config
+        self.max_num_reqs = max_num_reqs
+        self.max_num_tokens = max_num_tokens
+        self.max_rows = num_speculative_steps + 1
+        self.device = device
+        # The plan of a step that verifies drafts: today always a chain, with its
+        # counts and tokens in the runner's buffers. Other plans are laid out by
+        # layout, built by init_tree_verify.
+        self.chain_plan = VerifyPlan(
+            parent=chain_parents(max_num_reqs, self.max_rows, device),
+            count=None,
+            is_chain=True,
+        )
+        # The accepted path of every chain round, path[r, j] == j.
+        self.chain_path = chain_path(max_num_reqs, self.max_rows, device)
+        self.layout: PlanLayout | None = None
+        # What speculation holds (rows, decode graphs, branching), declared by
+        # the speculator's config. Memory is sized for it; set_resources lowers
+        # it to what the model's layers verify before capture.
+        self.resources = resources
+        self.capabilities: SpecCapabilities | None = None
+        # Above 1 the speculator verifies trees: every verify batch (chains and
+        # capture batches too) is laid out, so the attention metadata always
+        # carries tree_parents / tree_ancestors and one graph serves every plan.
+        self.max_branching = self.resources.max_branching
+        # The rows per request of a chain the runner lays out (max_branching > 1).
+        self.chain_count: torch.Tensor | None = None
+        if self.max_branching > 1:
+            self.chain_count = torch.ones(
+                max_num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device
+            )
+        # The spec verify and commit kernels (registry), bound by set_resources.
+        self.kernels: KernelRegistry | None = None
+        self.kernel_context: KernelContext | None = None
+        # Steps passed to BaseSpeculator.observe_step so far.
+        self.num_observed_steps = 0
+
+    def init_tree_verify(self, input_buffers: "InputBuffers") -> None:
+        """Buffers of a speculator whose plans branch."""
+        if self.max_branching == 1:
+            return
+        self.layout = PlanLayout(self.max_num_tokens, self.max_rows, self.device)
+        input_buffers.tree_parents = self.layout.tree_parents
+        input_buffers.tree_ancestors = self.layout.tree_ancestors
+
+    def registry(self) -> KernelRegistry:
+        """The speculator's spec kernels, built once per worker."""
+        if self.kernels is None:
+            self.kernels = KernelRegistry.from_config(self.vllm_config)
+        return self.kernels
+
+    def resolve_capabilities(self, runner: "GPUModelRunner") -> SpecCapabilities:
+        """What this rank's layers verify, after the attention backends are
+        built: the lowest plan kind of any target layer (draft layers do not
+        count), lowered to ``"chain"`` by each runner setting that keeps rows in
+        chain order."""
+        limits = layer_spec_limits(
+            runner.attn_groups,
+            runner.compilation_config.static_forward_context,
+            mamba_state_mode(runner.cache_config),
+            kernels=self.registry(),
+        )
+        settings = {
+            "pipeline parallelism (no tree path broadcast)": runner.use_pp,
+            "prefill context parallelism": runner.pcp_manager is not None,
+            "decode context parallelism": runner.dcp_size > 1,
+            "batch-sharded sampling": runner.batch_sharder is not None,
+            "micro-batching": runner.parallel_config.use_ubatching,
+            f"model state {type(runner.model_state).__name__}": (
+                not type(runner.model_state).supports_tree_verify
+            ),
+        }
+        limits += [
+            SpecLimit("chain", f"{what}: keeps verify rows in chain order")
+            for what, applies in settings.items()
+            if applies
+        ]
+        self.capabilities = SpecCapabilities.from_limits(limits)
+        return self.capabilities
+
+    def set_resources(
+        self,
+        resources: SpecResources,
+        input_buffers: "InputBuffers",
+        layers: list[SpecLayerSpec],
+    ) -> None:
+        """Run speculation with ``resources``, the engine core's adaptation of
+        the declared ones to what every rank verifies, and bind the spec kernels
+        to ``layers``. The memory stays sized for the declared resources."""
+        self.resources = resources
+        if resources.max_branching == 1 < self.max_branching:
+            # Lowered to chains: batches keep the chain layout.
+            self.max_branching = 1
+            self.chain_count = None

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The record a speculator receives after every sampled step."""
+
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config.compilation import CUDAGraphMode
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class StepObservation:
+    """What the model runner knows about a step once it has sampled.
+
+    Passed to ``BaseSpeculator.observe_step`` once per step that ran the
+    target forward and sampled, on the last pipeline-parallel rank: speculative
+    steps, steps with no drafts (candidate budget 1 included) and prefill
+    steps. Capture and profiling runs are not observed. Warm-up steps are,
+    because they run as scheduled steps.
+
+    Every field is something the runner already holds. Host values are ints
+    and numpy views of the step's input arrays; they stay valid until the
+    runner prepares the next step, so copy one to keep it. ``num_sampled`` and
+    ``num_rejected`` stay on the device: reading them on the host needs a
+    sync, so copy them asynchronously (``non_blocking`` into pinned memory,
+    then wait on an event) instead.
+    """
+
+    # Observed steps before this one on this runner, from 0.
+    step: int
+    # Host clock (time.perf_counter_ns()) when the runner began the step.
+    # GPU times are not recorded by the runner while serving: a consumer that
+    # wants them records its own CUDA events (the drafter of this step has not
+    # run yet when the step is observed).
+    start_ns: int
+    # Requests in the step, in batch row order.
+    req_ids: list[str]
+    num_reqs: int
+    # Request rows the forward ran, CUDA graph padding included.
+    num_reqs_padded: int
+    # Query tokens scheduled (drafts to verify included).
+    num_tokens: int
+    # Query tokens the forward ran, CUDA graph padding included.
+    num_tokens_padded: int
+    cudagraph_mode: CUDAGraphMode
+    # Query tokens per request when the batch was dispatched as uniform
+    # decode, else None.
+    uniform_token_count: int | None
+    num_ubatches: int
+    # Query tokens of requests that are still prefilling their prompt.
+    num_prefill_tokens: int
+    # Drafts the drafter proposes per request after this step: the candidate
+    # budget minus one. 0 when the budget is 1 (``skip_drafts``) or no DP rank
+    # can use drafts.
+    num_spec_tokens: int
+    # Host, per request: query tokens scheduled.
+    num_scheduled_tokens: np.ndarray
+    # Host, per request: tokens computed before this step.
+    num_computed_tokens: np.ndarray
+    # Host, per request: still prefilling its prompt.
+    is_prefilling: np.ndarray
+    # Host, per request: drafts verified this step (after the plan bound).
+    # None when no request carries drafts.
+    num_draft_tokens: np.ndarray | None
+    # Device, per request: tokens this step committed (accepted drafts and
+    # the bonus token) and scheduled query tokens it rejected.
+    num_sampled: torch.Tensor
+    num_rejected: torch.Tensor

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Verification of a plan that is not a chain: the walk down the tree.
+
+Every plan row gets the target's token. The walk then goes from the root to the
+child whose token equals the current row's target token, until a row has no such
+child. The accepted rows are the path (root first); the committed tokens are the
+target tokens of the path rows, the last of which is the bonus token.
+
+The default ``accept`` for such a plan takes the argmax, which is exact for greedy
+requests. A speculator that verifies sampled requests on trees overrides
+``accept`` and passes its own per-row target tokens to :func:`walk_tree`.
+"""
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.round import (
+    AcceptResult,
+    VerifyOutput,
+    VerifyPlan,
+)
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.sampler import Sampler
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _walk_tree_kernel(
+    target_ptr,  # [num_rows] int64: the target's token at every row
+    drafted_ptr,  # [num_rows] int64: each row's token, -1 never accepted
+    row_start_ptr,  # [R + 1] int32
+    parent_ptr,  # [R, C] int32
+    stride_parent,
+    count_ptr,  # [R] int32
+    sampled_ptr,  # [R, S] int64 out
+    stride_sampled,
+    path_ptr,  # [R, C] int32 out
+    stride_path,
+    path_len_ptr,  # [R] int32 out
+    C: tl.constexpr,
+    CP: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    b = tl.program_id(0)
+    start = tl.load(row_start_ptr + b)
+    num_rows = tl.minimum(
+        tl.load(row_start_ptr + b + 1) - start, tl.load(count_ptr + b)
+    )
+    rows = tl.arange(0, CP)
+    live = (rows > 0) & (rows < num_rows)
+    parent = tl.load(parent_ptr + b * stride_parent + rows, mask=rows < C, other=-1)
+    drafted = tl.load(drafted_ptr + start + rows, mask=live, other=-1)
+    target = tl.load(target_ptr + start + rows, mask=rows < num_rows, other=-1)
+    tl.store(path_ptr + b * stride_path + rows, rows, mask=rows < C)
+
+    node = 0
+    alive = num_rows > 0
+    length = 0
+    for step in range(0, C):
+        token = tl.sum(tl.where(rows == node, target, 0))
+        tl.store(sampled_ptr + b * stride_sampled + step, token, mask=alive)
+        tl.store(path_ptr + b * stride_path + step, node, mask=alive)
+        length += alive.to(tl.int32)
+        child = tl.min(tl.where(live & (parent == node) & (drafted == token), rows, CP))
+        alive = alive & (child < CP)
+        node = tl.where(alive, child, node)
+    tl.store(path_len_ptr + b, length)
+
+
+def walk_tree(
+    plan: VerifyPlan,
+    output: VerifyOutput,
+    target: torch.Tensor,
+    width: int | None = None,
+) -> AcceptResult:
+    """The accepted path of each request given ``target [num_rows]``, the
+    target's token at every row. ``sampled`` is ``[R, width]`` (default ``C``);
+    rows past ``plan.count`` and rows whose ``output.drafted`` is -1 are never
+    accepted."""
+    assert plan.count is not None
+    num_reqs, num_cols = plan.parent.shape
+    width = num_cols if width is None else width
+    assert width >= num_cols
+    device = target.device
+    sampled = torch.zeros(num_reqs, width, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
+    path = torch.empty(num_reqs, num_cols, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    path_len = torch.empty(num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    _walk_tree_kernel[(num_reqs,)](
+        target,
+        output.drafted,
+        output.row_start,
+        plan.parent,
+        plan.parent.stride(0),
+        plan.count,
+        sampled,
+        sampled.stride(0),
+        path,
+        path.stride(0),
+        path_len,
+        C=num_cols,
+        CP=triton.next_power_of_2(num_cols),
+        num_warps=1,
+    )
+    return AcceptResult(path=path, path_len=path_len, sampled=sampled)
+
+
+def accept_greedy_tree(
+    plan: VerifyPlan, output: VerifyOutput, sampler: "Sampler", width: int
+) -> AcceptResult:
+    """The default ``accept`` of a plan that is not a chain: the walk on the
+    argmax of each row's processed logits. Only greedy requests; a speculator
+    that verifies sampled trees overrides ``accept``."""
+    temperature = sampler.sampling_states.temperature.np[output.idx_mapping_np]
+    if not bool(np.all(temperature == 0.0)):
+        raise ValueError(
+            "a plan that is not a chain verifies sampled requests only through "
+            "the speculator's accept; the default accepts greedy requests"
+        )
+    processed = sampler.apply_sampling_params(
+        output.logits,
+        output.expanded_idx_mapping,
+        output.idx_mapping,
+        output.idx_mapping_np,
+        output.positions,
+        output.draft_tokens,
+        output.expanded_local_pos,
+        output.seq_lens_upper_bound_np,
+    )
+    result = walk_tree(plan, output, processed.argmax(dim=-1), width)
+    if processed is not output.logits:
+        result.processed_logits = processed
+    return result

🚀

I pushed a follow-up fix, `[Mamba] Capture full decode graphs for any uniform query length up to K+1`.

A speculator can declare decode shapes below 1 + K, for example a tree's chain fallback, and the CUDA graph manager captures one decode graph per declared shape. The Mamba capture builder asserted that the length equals 1 + K, so a Mamba2 hybrid such as Nemotron-H failed at startup with such a speculator. The decode path already takes any per-request length up to 1 + K, so the fix keeps only the existing upper bound, as GDN, short-conv and linear attention already do. Chain configs capture only 1 + K, as before. A builder test captures lengths 1, 2 and 4 with K = 3; lengths 1 and 2 fail without the fix.

With this change, a Nemotron TP4 tree speculator starts and serves 880 prompts. On one B300 (measured before the main merge, which does not touch these files), the 13 GPU test files listed in the description pass with the same counts (770 passed, 2 skipped) and `test_mamba_metadata_builder.py` passes 4 tests. `pre-commit`, mypy included, passes.

I also measured the PR against main on the same build: Qwen3.8-27B, TP4, B300, one vLLM wheel for both sides, 4 starts per arm, median tok/s with the min-max ratio range.

| | C1 | C8 | C64 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Speculation off, PR / main | 0.999x [0.996-1.050] | 0.991x [0.957-1.032] | 1.000x [0.932-1.058] |
| In-tree MTP K=3, PR / main | 0.994x [0.951-1.052] | 0.974x [0.816-1.042] | 0.968x [0.742-1.072] |

- The MTP C8 and C64 spread comes from one slow first start. Without it the ratios are 1.02x and 1.01x.
- Greedy outputs are identical on 20/20 prompts at C1 across all 8 starts, with speculation off and with MTP.
- At C64, outputs already differ between restarts of main itself, so I compare throughput only there.
- Mean acceptance length with MTP matches: 2.957 vs 2.957 at C1.
